title: Python Programming
description: Learn Python syntax and problem solving, build a command-line script, and establish reliable project habits.

paths.title: Python Basics
paths.description: Learn values, variables, conditions, loops, and functions.

paths.title: Build Your First Python Script
paths.description: Plan, implement, validate, and run a useful command-line program.

paths.title: Reliable Python
paths.description: Use collections, errors, modules, tests, and virtual environments.

cards.title: Python executes readable instructions
cards.prompt: Python is a general-purpose language used for automation, web services, data work, scientific computing, and scripting.
cards.content: Python emphasizes readable syntax, but clear names, small functions, and explicit error handling still require deliberate design.

cards.title: Create values and variables
cards.prompt: Variables bind names to objects so later instructions can reuse them.
cards.content: Python determines the runtime type from the assigned value. A name can be rebound, but changing types carelessly makes code harder to understand.

code.snippet:
course = "Python Basics"
lessons = 12
is_published = True
completion = 0.25

print(course, lessons, is_published, completion)

cards.title: Choose the list
cards.prompt: Which value is a Python list?

question.explanation: Square brackets create a list, an ordered mutable collection.

cards.title: Functions name reusable behavior
cards.prompt: A function groups instructions behind a name and can accept inputs and return an output.
cards.content: Small functions reduce repetition and make logic easier to test. A function should usually have one clear responsibility.

cards.title: Plan a study-time calculator
cards.prompt: Your first script will total study sessions and report whether a weekly target was reached.
cards.content: Define inputs and expected output before coding. This keeps the script focused and testable.
steps: Ask for the weekly target in hours.
Accept several session durations in minutes.
Compare the total with the target.

cards.title: Implement the calculator
cards.prompt: Parse comma-separated minutes, sum them, and compare the total with the target.
cards.content: Input returns text, so numeric conversion can fail. A later card adds validation.

code.snippet:
target_hours = float(input("Weekly target in hours: "))
raw_sessions = input("Session minutes, separated by commas: ")

minutes = [float(value.strip()) for value in raw_sessions.split(",")]
total_hours = sum(minutes) / 60

print(f"Studied: {total_hours:.2f} hours")
print("Target reached" if total_hours >= target_hours else "Keep going")

cards.title: Exceptions represent failed operations
cards.prompt: An exception interrupts normal execution when an operation cannot complete.
cards.content: Catch only errors you can handle meaningfully. A broad except that hides every failure makes debugging and data corruption more likely.

cards.title: Validate user input
cards.prompt: Handle invalid numbers and empty session lists without crashing.
cards.content: The function raises a specific message for invalid data, while the caller decides how to present the error.

cards.title: Dictionaries map keys to values
cards.prompt: A dictionary is useful when data has named fields or when values must be looked up by a unique key.
cards.content: Keys must be hashable. Dictionary access is typically clearer than relying on numeric positions for structured records.

cards.title: Modules organize code
cards.prompt: A module is a Python file that can expose functions, classes, and constants to other files.
cards.content: Use imports to separate interfaces, domain logic, storage, and tests. Avoid circular imports by keeping dependencies directional.

cards.title: Test a pure function
cards.prompt: A pure calculation is easy to test because its output depends only on its inputs.
cards.content: Tests protect expected behavior while allowing internal refactoring.

cards.title: Prepare a Python project
cards.prompt: Use an isolated environment and document how the program runs.
cards.content: Reproducible setup prevents one project’s dependencies from silently affecting another.
